subject: astronomy
title: Universe Calculations
welcome_lead: Work with light-years, distances and the immense scale of the universe.
meta_desc: GCSE Astronomy: galaxy distances, light-year calculations and universe scale.
final_note: Numbers in cosmology are huge — practice makes them manageable.

concepts.def: Distance light travels in one year, ~9.46 x 10^15 m.
Region of universe we can see, ~93 billion ly across.
Hundreds to thousands of galaxies bound by gravity.
Large structure of many galaxy clusters.
Large-scale pattern of filaments and voids.

walkthroughs.body_html: Speed of light is 3 x 10^8 m/s. Seconds in a year ~3.15 x 10^7. So 1 light-year = 3 x 10^8 x 3.15 x 10^7 ~ 9.46 x 10^15 m.
Milky Way ~10^5 ly across; Local Group ~10^7 ly across; observable universe ~9.3 x 10^10 ly across. Each step is ~1000x larger than the last.
If a galaxy is 100 million light-years away, we see it as it was 100 million years ago. The universe is a time machine.
